text:
marta: New report from a partner onboarding w/ our Next edge starter: using server components + client streaming triggers repeated embeddings and two auth refresh flows. Anyone looked into edge/server-components parity for the JS SDK? :thinking:
liam: Edge runtime + server components can behave like SSR but with different lifecycles. Repro steps?
marta: Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-edge-starter branch=edge-sc. Steps: pnpm i, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run dev (edge runtime), open /search. On first visit payload shows two POST /v1/embeddings and logs two "auth refresh start" entries.
jon: Can you paste the minimal server log?
marta: Log snippet: 

```
2026-01-12T11:02:10.100Z INFO server: render start route=/search
2026-01-12T11:02:10.105Z DEBUG embeddings: req=A1 input=question
2026-01-12T11:02:10.108Z DEBUG auth: refresh start id=R1
2026-01-12T11:02:10.150Z DEBUG embeddings: req=A2 input=question
2026-01-12T11:02:10.152Z DEBUG auth: refresh start id=R2
```

marta: A1/A2 identical payloads, R1/R2 separate refresh flows. We think server component rendered once and the client stream triggered the same pipeline, but the real issue is the SDK starts two refreshes rather than queuing one.
liam: That sounds like two SDK instances (edge server + browser) both trying to refresh  expected but annoying. But inside a single process we shouldn't have two concurrent refreshes for the same client instance. Are both calls coming from the same process?
marta: In edge runtime they appear in the same function trace (same process id in logs) which suggests the client instance itself allowed parallel refreshes. Could be a race when token is near-expiry and multiple requests trigger refresh concurrently.
jon: Short-term workaround for the starter I pushed: add an inflight-refresh mutex in lib/redwoodClient.ts and add an in-process embed coalescer for identical inputs. Patch: 

```ts
// lib/redwoodClient.ts
let inflightRefresh: Promise<void>|null = null;
async function refreshIfNeeded(){
  if(inflightRefresh) return inflightRefresh;
  inflightRefresh = (async ()=>{ /* perform refresh */ })();
  try{ await inflightRefresh } finally { inflightRefresh = null }
}
```

jon: And a simple embed dedupe map to avoid duplicate POSTs when server and client both call quickly.
liam: Good pragmatic fix. We should track this as an SDK parity bug: implement single-inflight auth refresh per client instance and optional request coalescing for embeddings.
sdk-bot: New issue created: SDK-1142 - js-sdk (edge): single-inflight auth refresh + embedding coalescing (https://tracker.redwood.ai/SDK-1142) :pager:
marta: I added a short note in the starter README: "Edge & server components: prefer server-only indexing or enable client dedupe to avoid duplicate embeddings; this is a known SDK parity gap."
ci-bot: Linked starter PR & CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/next-edge-starter/pull/5  tests added to assert only one POST /v1/embeddings on full page load.
jon: SDK follow-ups: 1) mutex for refresh per client instance; 2) opt-in coalescing for embeddings with a stable key function; 3) tests that simulate concurrent 401s and concurrent identical embedding calls.
liam: Also add docs in DevX guide about server components vs SSR vs client streaming patterns and sample snippets showing how to avoid duplicate network calls.
marta: Thanks all. Partner validated the starter with the workaround and onboarding went smoother. Will revert the local mutex/dedupe once SDK patch lands. Closing loop for now. :white_check_mark:
